figures.caption: Purification of the bioactive peptide from frozen chicken breast. The chromatographic profile of the chicken hydrolysate was obtained by RP-HPLC with a dC18 column. A peak indicated by an arrow shows the target peptide.
figures.label: Figure 1

figures.caption: ESI-TOF mass spectrum of the purified chicken peptide. Multiple charged molecular ions of the peptide were detected and indicated. The molecular mass of the peptide was calculated based on the most abundant peak.
figures.label: Figure 2

figures.caption: The prediction of the secondary structure of the chicken peptide. The prediction of the secondary structure was conducted by the GOR program on the Prabi server. c and e represent the secondary structure of random coil and exceeded strand, respectively.
figures.label: Figure 3

figures.caption: Aerobic plate count of the chicken breast treated with hydrolysate. Chicken breast samples were treated with beef, fish and chicken hydrolysates and then stored at 4 °C for 8 days. A sample without treatment served as a control. All the data are expressed as the mean + standard error derived from triplicate experiments. The chicken hydrolysate showed a significant difference at the p < 0.05 level in comparison with the control on day 4, indicated by asterisks.
figures.label: Figure 4

figures.caption: Enterobacteriaceae count of the chicken breast treated with hydrolysate. Chicken breast samples were treated with beef, fish and chicken hydrolysates and then stored at 4 °C for 8 days. A sample without treatment served as a control. Data are means + standard error derived from triplicate experiments. The chicken hydrolysate showed a significant difference at the p < 0.05 level in comparison with the control on day 4, indicated by asterisks.

figures.caption: LAB count of the chicken breast treated with hydrolysate. Chicken breast samples were treated with beef, fish and chicken hydrolysates and then stored at 4 °C for 8 days. A sample without treatment served as a control. Data are means + standard error derived from triplicate experiments. The fish hydrolysate showed a significant difference at the p < 0.05 level in comparison with the control on day 8, indicated by asterisks.
